:Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 27.10.2022 at about 8.30 a.m., the Petitioner was riding motor cycle bearing No.KA05ET9279 near 38th main road junction, 15th cross ring road, J.P.Nagar 6th phase.
At that time, a KIA car bearing No.KA02MR3839 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
He has spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as plumber and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car and therefore, Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further contended that the accident took place due to negligence of the petitioner himself.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further it denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further it contended that the driver of car was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle.
So also the rider of the two wheeler did not possess valid and effective driving licence.

Further it contended that the accident took place due to negligence of the petitioner and the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties i.e., the owner and insurer of Gangaiah.R vs Venu C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46702172/
2
the motor cycle involved in question.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 27.10.2022 at about 8.30 a.m. at 15th Cross Ring road, 38th main road junction,
J.P.Nagar, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of KIA car bearing No.KA02 MR3839?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If so, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3 . What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
He also examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P12 to 16 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.
8. Heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner.
The learned advocate also filed written arguments in support of his oral submission.
Heard the arguments of the learned advocate for respondent No.2.
I have carefully considered evidence both oral and documentary made available by the respective parties.
I have carefully considered the contents of written arguments.

My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 9.

Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 27102022 at about 8.30 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Regn.No.KA02 MR3839 by its driver.
10. On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Regn.No.KA02MR3839 by its driver.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P16.

sentences.text: Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot sketch, spot Mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and charge sheet.
Ex.P.8 is discharge summary, Ex.P.9 is the Medical bills, Ex.P.10 is the medical prescriptions and Ex.P.11 is the notarized copy of driving licence.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.1 & 2 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Jayanagar Traffic Police Station, the SHO of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of car bearing Regn.No.KA02MR3839 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC r/w Sec.134(B) of MV Act.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are Spot Mahazar along with sketch which justify the fact that IO has drawn the same in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles and also justify the fact of involvement of vehicles in question in the accident.
The document Ex.P.6 wound certificate shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

The document Ex.P.7 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Jayanagar Traffic Police Station has Chargesheeted the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC r/w Secs. 134(B), 187 of IMV Act.

13. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.S.U.Shivaprakash as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P.12 and 13 i.e.,
clinical notes and X ray.
PW.2 has reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
He also got examined Medical record officer as PW.3 and got marked Ex.14 to 16 i.e., case sheet, true copy of MLC extract and true copy of police intimation.
14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
15. Further, the Respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1.
RW.1 reiterated the Objection statement contentions in his chief affidavit.
In the cross examination, he admits that he is not an eyewitness to the accident.
There is also admission of the fact that IO has submitted charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle in question to which the respondent No.2 company has issued insurance policy.
There is admission of the fact that till date the said charge sheet is not challenged.

Though RW.1 stated to have issued a notice to the respondent No.2 to furnish the information as mentioned in para No.5 of the affidavit, admittedly said notice document is not produced before this court.
RW.1 admits that the policy in respect of the offending vehicle in question was valid and in force at the time of occurrence of accident.

The other suggestions have been denied by RW.1.
16.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, the oral evidence given by PW.1 corroborates the documentary evidence with regard to the proof of issue No.1.

Hence, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

4 17.
Issue No. 2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 48 years.
He has produced driving licence at Ex.P.11 to prove his age.
As per the driving licence, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 15.07.1977.
The accident took place on 27102022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 45 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
19. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as plumber and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to substantiate the said fact.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
21.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P6 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Closed Fracture BB right leg.
Closed fracture tibial condyle (L)
Further, the Doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
22.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
23.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 27.10.2022 to 29102022.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.S.U.Shivaprakash has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 3 days.
24. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/ under this head (@ Rs.15,500/ per month).
IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND Gangaiah.
R vs Venu C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46702172/

5 CONVEYANCE :
25.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
26. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.32,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.

In order to prove this fact, he has produced 36 medical bills i.e.,
Ex.P.9 which is totally amounting to Rs.1,40,235/.
There is no serious dispute about the medical bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,40,235/ which is rounded off to Rs.1,40,250/as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

27. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is suffering from severe pain at fractured area, cannot put weight on his both legs, cannot walk without support, cannot climb stairs, cannot fold his both legs,
cannot squat, cannot use Indian toilet, cannot lift any weight, cannot stand for more than 510 minutes, he limps while walking and using hand stick or walker to walk and his both legs have become fully disabled.

28. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.S.U.Shivaprakash as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Clinical examination notes and Xray at Ex.P.12 and 13.
He assessed physical disability of both lower limb at 67% and whole body disability at 34%.
29. In the crossexamination PW.2 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has admitted that he has not taken any opinion from the doctor who has treated the petitioner while assessing the disability.
He has also admitted that as per the recent Xray, fractures are united.
He has not seen follow up records.
He has also admitted that the petitioner is not suffering from any restrictions of movements of right hip and muscle power and the movements are normal.
There is also admission of the fact that only conservative treatment has been given for the left knee.

Hence,
having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering his age and the nature of work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 12% would be just and proper.
30. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 14.

With multiplier of 14, income of Rs.15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 12%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,12,480/ (Rs.15,500/ x 12 =
Gangaiah.R vs Venu C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46702172/
6 1,86,000/, Rs.1,86,000/x 14 x 12/100 = 3,12,480/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,12,480/ which is rounded off to Rs.3,12,500/ under this head.

FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
31.
In the petition, during his evidence the petitioner has stated that he needs to incur future medical expenses.
During his evidence, PW.2 deposed that in order to get the implants removed the petitioner might incur expenses of sum of Rs.30 to 40,000/ .
Though PW.2 has been cross examined at length, there is no suggestion also made thereby denying this aspect.
Record reveals that no documentary evidence are available to substantiate the quantum of such expense.

However,
considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, Tribunal finds it appropriate to award sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
This amount will not carry any future interest.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50.000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,40,250/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 31,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs. 3,12,500/
7.
Future Medical expenses Rs. 20,000/ Total Rs.5,98,750/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,98,750/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA 02MR3839.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of car.
The Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
34. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

7  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.5,98,750/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
